name: gdeltPyR
what_it_holds: 257-star, GPL-3.0 Python framework to retrieve full GDELT 1.0 and 2.0 Events tables (15-minute update cadence, back to 1979 for v1, 2015 for v2 events). Pulls raw event records (actors, event codes/CAMEO, geography, tone) into pandas, not just the Doc API subset.
why_useful: Lower-level than the Doc API client; would let a team filter GDELT Events by CAMEO codes/actor for tourism-, regulation-, or travel-related event categories (e.g. protest/legislation events tied to STR ordinances) rather than just keyword news volume. Addresses gap 14/17.
size_hint: no committed data; pull tool, GDELT itself is multi-TB
themes: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers
why_all: Lower-level than the Doc API client; would let a team filter GDELT Events by CAMEO codes/actor for tourism-, regulation-, or travel-related event categories (e.g. protest/legislation events tied to STR ordinances) rather than just keyword news volume. Addresses gap 14/17.

Could nowcast STR-regulation news flow, travel-shock events, or Airbnb-mention tone (gaps #12 regulation, #14 text/social, #17 methods) at daily/15-min granularity, filterable by CAMEO event codes and country/actor.

name: news-please
what_it_holds: General-purpose news crawler/extractor (headline, lead, text, image, author, date, language) that can crawl a given news site recursively or via RSS, and specifically supports pulling news articles out of Common Crawl's news archive (CC-NEWS). Apache-2.0, 820 commits.
why_useful: Could be pointed at Skift, PhocusWire, or other travel-trade press sites (or filtered against CC-NEWS) to build a travel-industry news corpus/timeline; also complements our existing Common Crawl CDX capture (different Common Crawl sub-index, CC-NEWS vs CDX/WARC).
last_activity: unknown exact date; 820 commits, long-running, widely used research tool
geography: any site the crawler is pointed at
time_coverage: CC-NEWS coverage from ~2016-present plus live crawling
duplicate_of_holding: adjacent to our existing Common Crawl CDX capture over airbnb.com, but this is the CC-NEWS route + generic site crawling, not the same index
themes: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers
why_all: Could be pointed at Skift, PhocusWire, or other travel-trade press sites (or filtered against CC-NEWS) to build a travel-industry news corpus/timeline; also complements our existing Common Crawl CDX capture (different Common Crawl sub-index, CC-NEWS vs CDX/WARC).

name: GDELT ecosystem (e.g. gdeltPyR, gdeltr2, spark-gdelt)
what_it_holds: 145 public repos tagged 'gdelt'; gdeltPyR (257 stars) is a Python client to pull GDELT 1.0/2.0 global event/news-tone data; gdeltr2 is the R equivalent; spark-gdelt runs GDELT through Apache Spark for large-scale event/news processing. All are acquisition tools over GDELT's own public data lake, not committed datasets.
why_useful: GDELT already flagged in CONTEXT gap #14 (text/social); these are the concrete, actively used client libraries (gdeltPyR in particular) that make a GDELT pull mechanical for a global news/event-tone or shock-detection feature (e.g. World Cup/conference/regulatory news spikes by country).
time_coverage: GDELT 1.0 (1979-) / 2.0 (2015-) as hosted by GDELT project
license: varies by repo (gdeltPyR: MIT-style, check repo)
last_activity: gdeltPyR last significant activity years ago per star history; topic page shows repos updated through 2026
themes: Event calendars: FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule and host-city data, Olympics, concerts (Setlist.fm, Songkick, Ticketmaster API), conferences, PredictHQ samples, holiday calendars by country
why_all: GDELT already flagged in CONTEXT gap #14 (text/social); these are the concrete, actively used client libraries (gdeltPyR in particular) that make a GDELT pull mechanical for a global news/event-tone or shock-detection feature (e.g. World Cup/conference/regulatory news spikes by country).

name: news-crawl
what_it_holds: Apache StormCrawler-based crawler that discovers articles via RSS/Atom feeds and Google News sitemaps and archives full article WARC content, feeding an ongoing AWS Open Dataset ('CC-NEWS') hosted by Common Crawl. Apache-2.0, 204 commits, actively maintained.
why_useful: CC-NEWS is a continuously updated, free, full-text news-article WARC corpus; filterable for Airbnb/short-term-rental/hospitality news mentions or regulation-tracker source articles (gap 12, gap 14 text/news) without needing a bespoke news scraper -- complements GDELT-style approaches.
geography: global, multi-language news sources with sitemaps/feeds
size_hint: CC-NEWS dataset is multi-TB overall; crawler repo itself is code only
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: CC-NEWS is a continuously updated, free, full-text news-article WARC corpus; filterable for Airbnb/short-term-rental/hospitality news mentions or regulation-tracker source articles (gap 12, gap 14 text/news) without needing a bespoke news scraper -- complements GDELT-style approaches.

name: Booking-com/absa-dataset (TRABL)
what_it_holds: TRABL: aspect-based sentiment analysis dataset from Booking.com covering three travel domains (hotels, attractions, destinations). 7,566 rows total (5,768 train / 898 validation / 900 test). Each row: review_id, two annotators' label sets (aspect_term, aspect_category, opinion_span, sentiment, supporting text snippet) built from LLM-generated labels with human correction. Average review ~42 words, ~7 aspect tuples/review. License CC-BY-SA-4.0 (non-commercial research). Accepted at ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW 2026).
why_useful: A structured, aspect-level sentiment dataset on hotel/attraction/destination reviews from a major OTA; marginal for KPI forecasting directly but could feed a text/sentiment nowcasting method (gap #14) if extended to a live pull, since it demonstrates a machine-labelable review schema.
time_coverage: Not stated; dataset published for WWW 2026
themes: Booking.com datasets beyond the 515k reviews: listing/price snapshots, alternative-accommodation counts, Booking scrapers, WSDM/RecSys Booking challenge data
why_all: A structured, aspect-level sentiment dataset on hotel/attraction/destination reviews from a major OTA; marginal for KPI forecasting directly but could feed a text/sentiment nowcasting method (gap #14) if extended to a live pull, since it demonstrates a machine-labelable review schema.
